title: test_support::MockBackend has unused inherent methods (e.g. new_with_account, force_create_error, clear_forced_create_error, state_for_test) where state_for_test exposes inner state via a MutexGuard — leaks the locking strategy across the test boundary
description:
What is awkward: lib.rs:234-236 exposes state_for_test() returning std::sync::MutexGuard<'_, HashMap<...>>. Tests then directly mutate the change log Vec to seed test fixtures — bypassing the trait methods entirely. This is a 'test pierce' that lets tests reach past the public API to manipulate internal state.

The mock backend is for testing, so loosening encapsulation is defensible. But state_for_test:
(a) exposes the std::sync::Mutex choice publicly, locking in that implementation detail across test code.
(b) The MutexGuard type is held across multiple .await points in some tests? — looking at the test code, no, the guard is dropped in the same scope. OK on await_holding_lock.

Suggested rewrite: replace state_for_test with explicit fixture-injection methods on MockBackend (e.g. record_created_id(account, id), record_destroyed_id, set_state). Each becomes a typed call that documents what it's doing. Tests do not need direct MutexGuard access — they need 'pretend account X has this change log'.

This is a refactor that would simplify the test surface significantly. Filing as P3 elegance.
